claim: Prenatal exposure to ethanol induces aberrant tangential migration of corticopetal GABAergic interneurons.
source: Prenatal exposure to ethanol induces aberrant tangential migration of corticopetal GABAergic interneurons, and long-term alterations in the form and function of the prefrontal cortex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Prenatal exposure to ethanol causes long-term alterations in the form and function of the prefrontal cortex.
source: Prenatal exposure to ethanol induces aberrant tangential migration of corticopetal GABAergic interneurons, and long-term alterations in the form and function of the prefrontal cortex.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Interneuronopathy contributes significantly to the pathoetiology of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD).
source: We have hypothesized that interneuronopathy contributes significantly to the pathoetiology of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis in the abstract.

claim: Activity-dependent tangential migration of GABAergic cortical neurons is driven by depolarizing responses to ambient GABA present in the cortical enclave.
source: Activity-dependent tangential migration of GABAergic cortical neurons is driven by depolarizing responses to ambient GABA present in the cortical enclave.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Ethanol exposure potentiates the depolarizing action of GABA in GABAergic cortical interneurons of the embryonic mouse brain.
source: We found that ethanol exposure potentiates the depolarizing action of GABA in GABAergic cortical interneurons of the embryonic mouse brain.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Pharmacological antagonism of the cotransporter NKCC1 mitigated ethanol-induced potentiation of GABA depolarization.
source: Pharmacological antagonism of the cotransporter NKCC1 mitigated ethanol-induced potentiation of GABA depolarization and prevented aberrant patterns of tangential migration induced by ethanol in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Pharmacological antagonism of NKCC1 prevented aberrant patterns of tangential migration induced by ethanol in vitro.
source: Pharmacological antagonism of the cotransporter NKCC1 mitigated ethanol-induced potentiation of GABA depolarization and prevented aberrant patterns of tangential migration induced by ethanol in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Maternal bumetanide treatment prevented interneuronopathy in the prefrontal cortex of ethanol exposed offspring.
source: In a model of FASD, maternal bumetanide treatment prevented interneuronopathy in the prefrontal cortex of ethanol exposed offspring, including deficits in behavioral flexibility.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Maternal bumetanide treatment prevented deficits in behavioral flexibility in ethanol exposed offspring.
source: In a model of FASD, maternal bumetanide treatment prevented interneuronopathy in the prefrontal cortex of ethanol exposed offspring, including deficits in behavioral flexibility.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: NKCC1 is a pharmacological target for the management of FASD.
source: These findings position interneuronopathy as a mechanism of FASD symptomatology, and posit NKCC1 as a pharmacological target for the management of FASD.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Binge-type exposure of the embryonic mouse brain to a moderate level of ethanol leads to interneuronopathy.
source: Binge-type exposure of the embryonic mouse brain to a moderate level of ethanol leads to interneuronopathy, hallmarked by aberrant tangential migration of corticopetal GABAergic interneurons derived from the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE) (Skorput et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to previous work.

claim: Interneuronopathy is hallmarked by aberrant tangential migration of corticopetal GABAergic interneurons derived from the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE).
source: Binge-type exposure of the embryonic mouse brain to a moderate level of ethanol leads to interneuronopathy, hallmarked by aberrant tangential migration of corticopetal GABAergic interneurons derived from the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE) (Skorput et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to previous work.

claim: Interneuronopathies are widely implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders.
source: Interneuronopathies are widely implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders (Catterall, 2018; Kato and Dobyns, 2005; Katsarou et al., 2017), including Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD) (Skorput et al., 2015; Skorput and Yeh, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: Self-reported rates of current drinking among pregnant women aged 18-44 years was 11.5% for the years 2015-2017.
source: Data from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System for the years 2015–2017 show self-reported rates of current drinking, and binge drinking (>4 drinks) within the past 30 days to be 11.5% and 3.9%, respectively, among pregnant woman aged 18–44 years.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction citing data from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System.

claim: Self-reported rates of binge drinking within the past 30 days among pregnant women aged 18-44 years was 3.9% for the years 2015-2017.
source: Data from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System for the years 2015–2017 show self-reported rates of current drinking, and binge drinking (>4 drinks) within the past 30 days to be 11.5% and 3.9%, respectively, among pregnant woman aged 18–44 years.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction citing data from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System.

claim: Pregnant binge drinkers averaged 4.5 binge episodes in the past 30 days with an average binge intensity of 6.0 drinks.
source: Pregnant binge drinkers averaged 4.5 binge episodes in the past 30 days with an average binge intensity of 6.0 drinks (Denny et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: The prevalence rates of FASD among first-graders in 4 US communities range from 1.1% to 5.0%.
source: As a result of such binge drinking episodes, FASD remains a major public health concern in the United States, and a recent assessment of first-graders in 4 US communities conservatively estimated the prevalence rates of FASD to range from 1.1% to 5.0% (May et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: The global prevalence rate of FASD is estimated at 7.7 per 1000 children.
source: The global prevalence rate of FASD is estimated at 7.7 per 1000 children, and is as high as 111.1 per 1000 children among some populations (Lange et al., 2017).

claim: The prevalence rate of FASD is as high as 111.1 per 1000 children among some populations.
source: The global prevalence rate of FASD is estimated at 7.7 per 1000 children, and is as high as 111.1 per 1000 children among some populations (Lange et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: The more efficacious current treatments for FASD rely primarily on postnatal behavioral therapy.
source: The more efficacious current treatments for FASD rely primarily on postnatal behavioral therapy (Nash et al., 2017), or pharmaceutics aimed to treat the symptoms, rather than the etiology, of this neurodevelopmental disorder (Peadon et al., 2009; Rowles and Findling, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Current treatments for FASD include pharmaceutics aimed to treat the symptoms, rather than the etiology, of this neurodevelopmental disorder.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: GABAergic neuroblasts arising in the MGE are fated to become parvalbumin (PV+) or somatostatin expressing inhibitory interneurons in the cortex.
source: GABAergic neuroblasts arising in the MGE are fated to become parvalbumin (PV+) or somatostatin expressing inhibitory interneurons in the cortex.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: Approximately 50% of MGE-derived population will mature to become PV+ fast-spiking basket cells.
source: Approximately 50% of this MGE-derived population will mature to become PV+ fast-spiking basket cells which are electrically coupled across the deep layers of the neocortex and pace oscillatory gamma rhythms, which are required for higher cognition (Batista-Brito and Fishell, 2009; Xu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: PV+ fast-spiking basket cells are electrically coupled across the deep layers of the neocortex and pace oscillatory gamma rhythms.
source: Approximately 50% of this MGE-derived population will mature to become PV+ fast-spiking basket cells which are electrically coupled across the deep layers of the neocortex and pace oscillatory gamma rhythms, which are required for higher cognition (Batista-Brito and Fishell, 2009; Xu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Oscillatory gamma rhythms are required for higher cognition.
source: Approximately 50% of this MGE-derived population will mature to become PV+ fast-spiking basket cells which are electrically coupled across the deep layers of the neocortex and pace oscillatory gamma rhythms, which are required for higher cognition (Batista-Brito and Fishell, 2009; Xu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Ethanol's positive allosteric modulation of GABAA receptors expressed on migrating neuroblasts is the mechanism by which in utero ethanol exposure causes enduring interneuronopathy in models of FASD.
source: Building on our previous work (Cuzon et al., 2008; Cuzon et al., 2006), we hypothesized that ethanol's positive allosteric modulation of GABAA receptors (GABAAR) expressed on migrating neuroblasts is the mechanism by which in utero ethanol exposure causes enduring interneuronopathy in models of FASD (Skorput et al., 2015; Skorput and Yeh, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis in the introduction with citations.

claim: In immature neurons, GABAA receptor activation results in membrane depolarization.
source: In these immature neurons, GABAAR activation results in membrane depolarization (Ben-Ari, 2014; Ben-Ari, 2002; Owens and Kriegstein, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Depolarizing GABAergic action has been postulated to drive the corticopetal tangential migration of GABAergic interneurons during corticogenesis.
source: This paradoxical depolarizing action has been postulated to drive the corticopetal tangential migration of GABAergic interneurons during corticogenesis (Behar et al., 1996; Ben-Ari, 2002; Ben-Ari et al., 2012; Cuzon et al., 2006; Wang and Kriegstein, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: NKCC1 is expressed at high levels in the embryonic brain when its activity predominates over that of the chloride exporting K+-Cl- co-transporter (KCC2).
source: To this end, we targeted the chloride importing Na+-K+−2Cl- isoform one cotransporter (NKCC1) because it is expressed at high levels in the embryonic brain when its activity predominates over that of the chloride exporting K+-Cl- co-transporter (KCC2).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: The differential activity of NKCC1 and KCC2 results in a net higher [Cl-]i compared to [Cl-]o.
source: This differential activity results in a net higher [Cl-]i compared to [Cl-]o.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: The reversal potential for chloride (EGABA) is set at a membrane potential that is depolarized relative to the resting membrane potential in embryonic neurons.
source: As such, the reversal potential for chloride, and that of GABA-activated responses (EGABA), is set at a membrane potential that is depolarized relative to the resting membrane potential.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction.

claim: GABAA receptor activation causes chloride extrusion and membrane depolarization in migrating neuroblasts.
source: Thus, GABAAR activation causes chloride extrusion and membrane depolarization in these migrating neuroblasts (Ben-Ari, 2014; Ben-Ari, 2002; Owens and Kriegstein, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Bumetanide is an NKCC1 antagonist that shifts the EGABA of embryonic neuroblasts to a more negative membrane potential when administered maternally.
source: The loop diuretic bumetanide is an NKCC1 antagonist that shifts the EGABA of embryonic neuroblasts to a more negative membrane potential when administered maternally (Wang and Kriegstein, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation.

claim: The timing of gestational exposure to ethanol is a key determinant of the diagnostic outcome of FASD.
